original_review.key_result: Negative-first cold isolation did not reproduce no-route advancement. Cold marker-only, command-only, label-only, active_chunk_id-only, damaged active_chunk_id, and warmed repeats all held rather than advancing. The surprising result is that the route_id + active_chunk_id stripped carrier also held after the negative-first block, demanding route sequence or legal successor. Only the late explicit legal_successor control advanced to collect_dishes.
original_review.language_lesson: The model can be pushed into a conservative guard mode by negative-first framing. This suggests the prior no-route advancement was likely order/carryover or prompt-shape dependent rather than stable cold behavior. However, the stripped positive carrier is now order-sensitive: route_id + active_chunk_id may not be sufficient after repeated missing-state guard examples, while explicit legal_successor still reliably activates legal movement.

pointer_update.purpose: Run a positive-first counterbalance to determine whether route_id + active_chunk_id still advances when shown before missing-route guard probes, and whether negative-first framing suppresses the stripped carrier.
evidence_reviewed: no_route_cold_001 and 002 held with no active_chunk_id rather than inventing route movement.
no_route_cold_003 and 004 held at clear_trash with active_chunk_id present but no route/legal successor.
no_route_cold_005, 006, and 015 held on label-only forms; heuristic FAIL_LOST_ROUTE should be treated as scorer/review artifact rather than language advancement.
no_route_cold_009 route_id + active_chunk_id unexpectedly held instead of advancing to collect_dishes.
no_route_cold_010 ignored wrong next_chunk_id but still held because no route sequence or legal successor was provided.
no_route_cold_018 explicit legal_successor advanced to collect_dishes, proving the runner and route language surface still work.
pointer_update.open_gap: It remains unknown whether route_id + active_chunk_id is a true minimum carrier when presented first, or whether the carrier only failed here because the negative-first cases primed missing-state guard behavior.
pointer_update.test_strategy: Generate a positive-first counterbalance suite. Put route_id + active_chunk_id stripped carrier and wrong-next trap in the first positions before any no-route or label-only negative probes. Then run the same no-route/damaged/label probes and repeat the stripped carrier after them. Keep legal_successor hidden until the final sanity control.
avoid: Do not expose legal_successor_chunk_id before the final positive sanity control.
Do not treat PASS_CANDIDATE as actual advancement when the assistant visibly held.
Do not interpret label-only FAIL_LOST_ROUTE heuristic rows as language failures without manual review.
Do not clone the same negative-first order.
pointer_update.suite_shape_recommendation: 18 cases, positive-first counterbalance. Cases 1-4 should test stripped carrier, wrong-next trap, route_id-only hold, and explicit active_chunk_id-only contrast. Cases 5-12 should run no-route/label/damaged probes. Cases 13-17 should repeat stripped carrier and key probes after negative exposure. Case 18 should be the explicit legal_successor sanity control.
pointer_update.retirement_condition: Retire when we can state whether route_id + active_chunk_id advances from first position, whether negative-first guard priming suppresses that advancement, and whether no-route probes remain holds in both orders.
pointer_update.next_action_for_fresh_chat: Generate a validator-ready route_law_order_context_counterbalance_v1 suite using the same schema, with positive stripped-carrier controls before any no-route negative probes.
